presentation._comment_shadow_opacity: Stormwood's scene authors a 0.68 canopy-shadow floor for its permanent storm. WorldLook reapplies the global sun defaults after scene setup, so every phase must carry that realm-local value explicitly; Break alone returns to fully hard shadows, as the surge brief specifies.
presentation._comment_reapply: WorldLook re-merges its whole look per set_weather call, so the weather layer is re-applied every reapply_fading_seconds during a cross-fade and every reapply_steady_seconds otherwise (to follow the day clock). The ceiling updates every frame.
presentation._comment_floors: Review R2-2 / round-2 judge (a),(b): the storm horizon (and fog, which equals it) never falls below horizon_fraction of the native horizon luminance for the hour, and the ceiling never below ceiling_fraction of it, keeping each phase's authored hue. Night Break stays violet-indigo instead of sinking to black; day Break's sky reads as a storm afternoon, not night. Ceilings are fully opaque (no sun/moon ghost through them); only Fading's breakup opens gaps, and only by day.
presentation._comment_rain: Stormwood's own rain emitter (world_weather.gd builds it hidden and Meadows-sized). The near layer is centred horizontally on the ACTIVE CAMERA and vertically on the ground: it spawns in spawn_band_above_ground_m over the higher of the terrain under the camera and the trainer, and lives lifetime_s, so drops fall through the foreground instead of the old camera-centred 14 m column where a measured 72-75% of drops were underground and ~2% reached the bottom 45% of the frame (WO-F10-07). max_drops is the Break (amount 1.0) count; each phase's rain_amount scales it. Streaks are thin tapered translucent spindles (streak_width_m is the base diameter) that fade in/out over life (fade_in/out_fraction); wind_slant tilts the fall (x, z per unit of fall) and streaks align to their velocity. The ring is shifted upwind by upwind_offset_fraction of the drift and its inner radius is derived as lens_clearance_m + the larger drift share + the 2-degree spread drift + the streak's sideways half-extent, ring_width_m wide; unit tests hold every drop >= 1.5 m from the lens, check rain reaches within 3 m of the trainer and that the foreground (bottom 45% of the view) gets rain. A physics roof over the camera's framed subject or the camera fades the near layer out over roof_fade_seconds (canopy and rod radius ignored). The emitter never sits more than max_height_above_ground_m above that floor; camera_height_offset_m is the fallback when the ground is unknown. far_layer (explicit radii, own lifetime/height, centre_offset_m above the near centre) is shorter and fainter. At night each layer's tint follows the night factor down to its night_floor and alpha drops to its night_alpha_fraction; the near layer keeps a higher floor so night rain reads over the grass, the far layer a low one so the sky never looks like snow.
presentation._comment_telegraph: The strike warning uses the game's one hazard colour, read at runtime from combat.json telegraph.colour (magenta; see its _why_colour_0905: white-violet read as a heal/selection circle and amber as reward gold, here as in combat). Rim exactly at strike.radius_m, a glow of the same colour for edge_falloff_m past it, a dark interior (fill_colour) that darkens the ground as the strike nears, a pulse chirping pulse_hz_start->pulse_hz_end over strike.telegraph_seconds, and a white-hot core on impact. Only the rim and glow are pulled depth_pull_m (about grass height) toward the camera, never the fill, so the fill cannot draw over a trainer at the near rim. One cached indexed mesh; per strike only the centre and 16 rim heights are sampled.
presentation._comment_storm_base: OWNER DIRECTION (WO-F10-08): 'We should not have day and night in stormwood. It should just always be that kind of purple rainy sky regardless of time of day', including after the Long Storm is broken. stormwood_surge.gd hands this realm's WorldLook a config in which every time-of-day preset is reference_time plus overrides, so sky, clouds, fog, ambient, exposure and the key light's angle, energy and colour are the same at every hour; the world clock, is_dark(), night rest and encounter timing keep running. pin_time_of_day false restores the clock-blended look. The overrides keep the painted clouds and sun colour in the purple family.
presentation._comment_phases: OWNER DIRECTION (WO-F10-08, round 2): 'I like the building and break pictures. The other two aren't fantastic enough.' Every phase and the aftermath now sit in the deep purple family of Building and Break (sky, ceiling, fog, key and ambient level); nothing pale lavender or grey. Phases are nameable without HUD text by: rain amount (Calm 0.4, Building 0.65, Break 1.0, Fading 0.15, aftermath 0.08) and wind slant (`wind` 0.45 / 0.85 / 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.3 of the configured maximum); ceiling motion and churn (ceiling_speed 0.008 / 0.03 / 0.045 / 0.014 / 0.002, contrast 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.55 / 0.3 / 0.12); lightning (Break: strikes, sky flashes and strong in-cloud sheet_glow; Building: faint sheet_glow only; others none); fog density and key/ambient level darkest in Break (ground follows the storm, blind judge 2). `intensity` (0..1) is a read-only hook for other presentation (surge_intensity()). fog_colour follows sky_horizon (art.json's seam rule). No red: oxblood is Team Tether's.
presentation._comment_aftermath: OWNER RULING (WO-F10-08): Stormwood stays purple after the Long Storm is broken; 'the aftermath shows only through lighter rain, no lightning and the scars'. Round 2: the same deep purple family as Break, not pale. Every aftermath phase (`all`) is the stillest version: the lightest drizzle (0.08), the gentlest wind (0.3), an almost still ceiling (speed 0.002, contrast 0.12), no flashes or sheet glow, the least fog and a steady key. The shorter aftermath Surge durations (aftermath_seconds) are unchanged gameplay; real strikes in an aftermath Break still telegraph and strike (rules), but no ambient flashes are added.
presentation._comment_flash: Break's flash rhythm (ART_DIRECTION 3.3 'flash rhythm', 4 'white-violet lightning'). Distant sky flashes carry no telegraph, so they are clearly weaker than a real strike's full flash (distant_strength_min..max, echo double_strength, all <= 0.35 of a strike) and on their own slower cadence (distant_interval_min..max, 9-16 s, apart from the 4-8 s strike spacing): a flash without a ring must never read as a missed warning. A strike impact always draws its bolt and local light at the impact; its whole-sky flash is full only while the local presentation is Break, otherwise it fades with distance from the local player to zero at strike_sky_range_m (glass-sink strikes happen in any phase and are broadcast to every peer). UX 8 reduced motion multiplies every sky flash (distant and strike) by reduced_motion_scale; the strike's local light is scaled by the same factor, the telegraph rim stops pulsing (its growing fill keeps the timing), and the ring and bolt themselves are gameplay tells and are unchanged. reduced_motion_scale is 0.15 rather than the 0 that motion_prefs.impulse_scale() uses for camera impulses: the flash rhythm is one of the cues that make Break nameable without HUD text (WORLD 5.2, ART_DIRECTION 3.3), and UX 8 asks reduced motion to LOWER non-essential flashes, so a faint, slow brightening is kept rather than removing Break's light cue entirely. strike_* are the impact's bolt and light in stormwood_lightning.gd.
